entities.summary:
Giovanni Cimabue, also known as Cenni di Pepo or Cenni di Pepi, was an Italian painter and designer of mosaics from Florence.

Born around 1240, Cimabue is considered one of the most important artists of the International Gothic style, which emphasized elegance, refinement, and emotional depth. His work had a profound influence on the development of Renaissance art, particularly in Italy.

Cimabue's innovative use of gold and his mastery of color and light earned him widespread recognition during his lifetime. His most famous works include the 'Scrovegni Chapel' frescoes and the 'San Zeno' mosaics.

Despite his significant contributions to the art world, Cimabue's life and work are not as well-documented as those of his contemporaries. Nevertheless, his legacy continues to inspire artists and art historians to this day.

Cimabue's artistic style was characterized by its subtlety and nuance, often conveying complex emotions through subtle expressions and gestures. His work also showcased a deep understanding of classical Greek and Roman art, as well as the Byzantine tradition.

This enigmatic artist's mysterious life and untimely death at the age of 62 remain shrouded in controversy, with some art historians questioning the accuracy of Cimabue's biography. Nevertheless, his artistic achievements continue to captivate audiences around the world.

In 2004, Cimabue's 'Scrovegni Chapel' frescoes were recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, cementing his status as one of the most important artists of the Middle Ages.
